Kebbi State Governor, Nasir Idris, has reinstated the Commissioner for Animal Health, Husbandry and Fisheries, Alhaji Kabir Usman Alaramma, four months after he was suspended from office. The reinstatement, which takes immediate effect, was announced on Monday by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Alhaji Yakubu Ahmed-BK, shortly after the State Executive Council meeting presided over by the governor at the Government House, Birnin Kebbi. Ahmed-BK said the governor had directed that the suspension imposed on Alaramma be lifted, paving the way for his immediate return to office. “Consequently, he has been reinstated to his position and is hereby directed to resume his official duties with immediate effect,” the commissioner said. Alaramma was suspended in June 2026 by the state government, although the government did not publicly provide specific details of the allegations against him. However, the government did not state whether Alaramma’s reinstatement followed the conclusion of an investigation or any other administrative process. The Ministry of Animal Health, Husbandry and Fisheries plays a significant role in Kebbi’s agricultural economy, with responsibilities covering livestock development, animal disease control, veterinary services, fisheries production and pastoralist affairs. Kebbi is endowed with substantial livestock and fisheries resources, making the ministry central to the state’s efforts to improve animal production, strengthen food security and expand agricultural opportunities. The state government said the reinstatement reflected its commitment to effective governance, administrative responsibility and sustained engagement with political stakeholders across the state. Alaramma is expected to resume his responsibilities as a member of the State Executive Council following the governor’s directive. Animashaun Salman
